_readme: The corpus both halves of the image lane are held to: src/core/imageCandidate.ts and
scraper/images.py must return the SAME key and the SAME refusal for every URL here.
Every entry is a real string taken from runs/acquired/ (the source is named), not an invented
one - a suite made only of clean inputs certifies the easy half of the problem.
key: what url_key() must return (null = not fetchable).
placeholder: the refusal placeholderReason() must give, or null when the URL is fetchable.
note: why this case is in the corpus.

cases.note: provantage, the ordinary case: a real product photo, upper-case extension
router-switch: a CATEGORY banner no substring can recognise. It is refused by the count rule (max_parts_per_url_key), not here - which is exactly why placeholder is null.
router-switch prints every photo twice; the transcode must give the SAME key as the line above or the lane spends two requests on one picture
meraki: the size lives in the query, so the query is dropped from the key and read as a hint instead
the same meraki file at a larger rendition: one candidate, and the lane must fetch THIS one
hpe-quickspecs prints the COMPANY LOGO in the same image block as the product shot
the product shot from the same page must NOT be refused: 'img' is not 'logo'
a file whose EXTENSION is a stripped segment name; the filename is never stripped
adversarial: rendition segments named like the file. Directories go, the filename stays.
a SERIES banner that is also the only photo Arista gives. No '/banner/' substring exists on purpose; the count rule decides.
Magento's own placeholder path, served with a 200 and a real JPEG body
layout spacer; a valid GIF that sniff() would happily accept
site chrome scraped as a product image
'catalog' contains 'log' but not 'logo': the substring list must not swallow every catalogue URL there is
an inline image is not something this lane can fetch and must never become a row
a relative src an adapter forgot to resolve

_sku_readme: sku_cases: the names-another-sku rule, which refuses a filename naming a SIBLING model and
accepts one naming the part's OWN FAMILY. Both halves are held to this list -
scraper/images.py other_sku_reason() and src/core/imageCandidate.ts otherSkuReason() - and
tests/imageCandidate.test.ts compares the two verdict for verdict.
The first fourteen are the entire real corpus: every image_candidate the supervised batch
(run #50, 4 Sep 2026) refused with names-another-sku, URL and SKU as stored. Six of them were
the family photo and were wrong to refuse; eight name another model and stay refused.
sku      the part whose page the image was on.
known    the filename tokens that are real parts.sku rows for this vendor - what
known_sku_map() would return. Every SKU here except C9200/C9200L/MR55 is a real row
in the catalogue as of 4 Sep 2026; those three are named in their case notes.
verdict  the reason both halves must return, or null when the candidate is accepted.

sku_cases.note: REAL, still refused. The named token is LONGER than ours: MG41E is the external-antenna gateway, a descendant and never a family. Direction matters.
REAL, still refused. Same length, different model digits: a sibling wall AP.
REAL, still refused. The refusal the rule was written for: meraki serves MR45.png as the MR46 page's primary image.

REAL, still refused, and the reason CHANGES from MS120 to MS120-24. The file names our family AND a 24-port sibling; a sibling refuses even when the family is also named, and the reason must name the sibling or it sends the operator to look at the wrong thing.

REAL, still refused, deliberately and at a cost: 'MS125-24-PoE' is very likely this exact switch spelled out, but MS125-24 is a real non-PoE sibling and MS125-24P is not MS125-24 plus a dash. A wrong picture is worse than a recorded gap.
REAL, now ACCEPTED. The file calls itself the MS130 family photo and MS130-8 extends MS130 across a dash.
REAL, now ACCEPTED. The family photo, refused by run #50 only because MS210 is also a row in parts.
REAL, now ACCEPTED. MS225-48 is a real sibling but this filename does not name it - only MS225 does.
REAL, still refused. MS250-48 is the non-PoE 48-port switch; MS250-48LP glues LP on with no dash, so it is a variant and not a configuration. The two look alike and it is refused anyway.
REAL, now ACCEPTED. The third of the three family photos named in the brief.

REAL, still refused, and the case that shows why 'accept the family' cannot be the whole rule: this file names the MS355 family AND two specific models, neither of which is the MS355-24X whose page it was on. MS355.png on the same page would be accepted - same part, different file, different verdict.
REAL, now ACCEPTED.
REAL, now ACCEPTED.
REAL, still refused. MX64W is the MX64 with radios and visible antennas - a different chassis, and the W is glued on with no dash.
TIE CASE from the brief: MS350 vs MS350-24P, accept as family.
TIE CASE from the brief: MS355-24X vs MS355.png, accept as family. The sibling MS355-24X2 exists but this filename does not name it.
TIE CASE from the brief: MR44 vs MR46, refuse. Same length, differs only in the model digits.

TIE CASE from the brief: MX67 vs MX67C, REFUSE. Meraki reserves the dash for the port/PoE configuration of one chassis and an appended letter for a different chassis - the C carries an integrated LTE modem and its antennas. MX67 and MX67C also have ZERO dash-children each in the catalogue, i.e. both are leaves, while MS210 has 10 and C9200L 119.

TIE CASE from the brief: C9200L-24P-4G vs C9200L.png, accept as family. C9200L is not itself a row in parts today, so in production this filename names nothing and is accepted anyway - the case pins the RULE, not today's catalogue.

SABOTAGE, another family sharing a prefix letter pattern: C9200 is the Catalyst 9200 and C9200L the 9200L, different switches. A naive startswith() accepts this; requiring the dash boundary refuses it. C9200 is not a parts row today either - the case exists so the guard cannot be removed unnoticed.

SABOTAGE, and the reason parts.family is NOT an accept criterion: MS250 and MS225-48FP carry the SAME parts.family ('Cisco Meraki'), so a rule that accepted a token matching the part's family would put a photo of an MS250 on the MS225-48FP page.

The one place the descendant direction is NOT refused, recorded because it is an artefact and not a decision: sku_tokens splits ms210-24p into MS210-24P and MS210, so the file names our own SKU and 'names this part' wins. It is harmless here - MS210 is a family row and the photo is of a model inside it - and it cannot leak to a sibling, because a sibling's filename never contains our SKU as a dash-separated piece (MS410-16 <- ms410-32.jpg is still refused). The genuine descendant case, MG41 <- MG41E.png, has no dash and IS refused.
the sibling case that proves the artefact above cannot leak: the file names our family (MS410) and a sibling (MS410-32) but never our own SKU, so the sibling refuses.
a filename that names THIS part is not refused

meraki's hardware-only SKU is the same product as its PID. Accepted twice over: sku_equivalent_suffixes makes the relation 'same', and sku_tokens emits MR46 alongside MR46-HW so 'names this part' would carry it anyway. The redundancy is recorded, not relied on - see the sabotage in tests/scraper/test_image_rules.py.

-HW is meraki's hardware-only SKU for the same product, so MR46.png on the MR46-HW page is this part's own photo. Without sku_equivalent_suffixes this reads as 'another part we hold' - MR46 IS a separate row.
the SKU comparison ignores the punctuation a PID carries: C9200L-24P-4G= is the same part
a photo of two products, one of them ours, is not refused. MR55 is a real meraki AP but not a row in the catalogue today.
a filename that names nothing in the catalogue is not refused: only a POSITIVE identification refuses
